summary: Recent updates to the WebCodecs area of the Firefox browser focused on improving how video frames are handled, particularly in terms of copying and cropping data. A key change was the renaming of a function to better reflect its purpose, which now more accurately describes how it transfers specific data planes of video frames. Additionally, the updates enhance the efficiency of cropping operations by ensuring that only the visible portion of video frames is processed, which can lead to smoother performance during video playback. These enhancements contribute to a more reliable experience when working with video content on the web, ultimately ensuring users encounter fewer errors and better-quality visuals. **Overall, these changes aim to make video processing faster and more efficient, significantly benefiting developers and users alike.**
